title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 9 questions (9.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A network team asks which firewall rules a virtual appliance needs to talk to Identity Security Cloud. What is the BEST answer?
choices: Outbound HTTPS on port 443 to the cloud, with no inbound internet rules
Inbound HTTPS on port 443 from the tenant to the VA's public IP address on the edge
Inbound SSH on port 22 so the tenant can push jobs to the VA
Two-way LDAP on port 389 between the tenant and the VA
questions.answer: Outbound HTTPS on port 443 to the cloud, with no inbound internet rules
questions.explanation: The VA starts every connection outbound over HTTPS, so no inbound internet rule is needed. LDAP and similar ports are only needed from the VA to on-premises sources.

questions.stem: How does an on-premises virtual appliance receive an aggregation job started in the tenant?
choices: The VA polls cloud message queues and picks up the job
The tenant opens a connection into the data center and pushes the job
The tenant emails the job to a mailbox the VA reads every hour
A source owner downloads the job and copies it onto the VA
questions.answer: The VA polls cloud message queues and picks up the job
questions.explanation: Work is placed on queues that the VA polls, which is why only outbound access is needed. The cloud never connects into the customer network.

questions.stem: An engineer types an Active Directory service account password into a VA-based source. How is that credential protected?
choices: It is stored in plain text in the tenant and masked in the user interface
It is encrypted with the VA cluster's public key
It is encrypted with the engineer's personal access token secret
It is copied to every tenant in the region for redundancy
questions.answer: It is encrypted with the VA cluster's public key
questions.explanation: Source credentials for VA connectors are encrypted with the cluster key pair, and the private key stays on the VAs. SailPoint's cloud cannot read the password.

questions.stem: Corporate policy forces all outbound web traffic through an HTTP proxy. What must the engineer do so the VA can reach the cloud?
choices: Open an inbound port so the tenant can reach the VA directly
Install a second VA outside the proxy and route the first through it
Configure the VA's proxy settings for its outbound connections
Change every source to a direct connector so no VA is used
questions.answer: Configure the VA's proxy settings for its outbound connections
questions.explanation: VAs support a proxy configuration for their outbound traffic. Opening inbound ports does not help, because the VA always starts the connection.

questions.stem: A VA cannot connect to the cloud after the security team turned on TLS inspection for all outbound traffic. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Exclude the VA's traffic to SailPoint endpoints from TLS inspection
Replace the VA's certificate with the inspection appliance's certificate
Move the VA to the same subnet as the inspection appliance
Turn off encryption on the VA's connection to the cloud
questions.answer: Exclude the VA's traffic to SailPoint endpoints from TLS inspection
questions.explanation: Intercepting and re-signing the VA's TLS sessions breaks its secure channel, so SailPoint traffic must bypass inspection. Turning off encryption is not possible or acceptable.

questions.stem: A cluster has three VAs and one is offline for patching. What happens to new jobs for that cluster's sources?
choices: The remaining healthy VAs pick up the queued jobs
The jobs wait until all three VAs are back online
The jobs are sent to another customer's cluster in the region
The tenant runs the jobs in the cloud without any VA
questions.answer: The remaining healthy VAs pick up the queued jobs
questions.explanation: VAs in a cluster share the same queues, so any healthy member takes the work. Jobs never move to clusters of other tenants.

questions.stem: A company adds a SaaS application whose connector runs entirely in SailPoint's cloud. What does this mean for the integration's network path?
choices: The VA must relay every call from the cloud to the SaaS provider's API
The SaaS application must open an inbound port to the VA
The SaaS application must poll the tenant's message queues
The cloud calls the SaaS API directly, with no VA in the path
questions.answer: The cloud calls the SaaS API directly, with no VA in the path
questions.explanation: Direct (cloud) connectors call the SaaS service from SailPoint's cloud. VAs are needed for sources that are only reachable inside the customer network.

questions.stem: An engineer must choose between trigger types for an integration. Which statement describes a fire-and-forget trigger?
choices: The platform pauses the process until the subscriber returns a decision
The subscriber must answer within a set time or the process fails
The event is sent and the platform does not wait for a reply
The event is held until an Admin releases it from the dashboard
questions.answer: The event is sent and the platform does not wait for a reply
questions.explanation: Fire-and-forget triggers notify subscribers and carry on. Request-response triggers wait for the subscriber's answer before continuing.

questions.stem: An external risk engine must decide whether an access request may proceed before approvers see it. Which trigger type fits?
choices: A fire-and-forget trigger such as identity created, with a filter
A request-response trigger such as access request pre-approval
A scheduled workflow that runs each night
A search subscription sent to the risk team
questions.answer: A request-response trigger such as access request pre-approval
questions.explanation: Request-response triggers pause until the subscriber replies with a decision, which suits pre-approval. Fire-and-forget events cannot influence the outcome.

questions.stem: The security team wants identity events delivered into its AWS account for processing. Which subscription type should the engineer use?
choices: An HTTP subscription to the VA
An Amazon EventBridge subscription
A search subscription
An email template
questions.answer: An Amazon EventBridge subscription
questions.explanation: Event triggers support EventBridge subscriptions that deliver events to a partner event source in the customer's AWS account. An HTTP subscription would need a reachable web endpoint.

questions.stem: An HTTP subscription endpoint must reject calls that do not come from Identity Security Cloud. What should the engineer configure?
choices: A personal access token on the endpoint's own server
Basic or bearer token authentication on the HTTP subscription
A trigger filter that checks the caller's IP address on each event
The VA proxy settings for the endpoint host
questions.answer: Basic or bearer token authentication on the HTTP subscription
questions.explanation: HTTP subscriptions can send basic or bearer credentials that the receiver checks. Filters choose which events are sent; they do not authenticate the caller.

questions.stem: A subscriber needs several minutes to reach a decision on a request-response trigger. Which response approach is BEST?
choices: Use a synchronous response and keep the connection open for the whole time
Use an asynchronous response sent later to the callback in the event
Switch the trigger to fire-and-forget and decide afterwards
Return an empty reply at once and email the decision
questions.answer: Use an asynchronous response sent later to the callback in the event
questions.explanation: Async mode lets the subscriber acknowledge at once and send the decision to the callback before the deadline. A long synchronous call risks timing out.

questions.stem: An HTTP subscription points at an internal web server with no internet access, and no events arrive. Why?
choices: Events are only sent through the VA, which lacks the right proxy settings
HTTP subscriptions accept only endpoints hosted in AWS
Internal servers need the Admin user level to receive events
Events come from SailPoint's cloud, so the endpoint must be reachable
questions.answer: Events come from SailPoint's cloud, so the endpoint must be reachable
questions.explanation: Event trigger delivery comes from SailPoint's cloud, so an internal-only server cannot receive it. A reachable HTTPS endpoint or EventBridge is needed.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to check an HTTP subscription's endpoint handling before real events flow. What is the BEST step?
choices: Wait for the next production event and read the logs
Create a temporary identity in production to cause an event
Run an unoptimized aggregation on every source
Send a test invocation with the trigger's sample payload
questions.answer: Send a test invocation with the trigger's sample payload
questions.explanation: Test invocations send a sample payload to the subscription so the receiver can be checked safely. Creating fake production data is disruptive.

questions.stem: A script must request an access token for the tenant acme. Which URL is valid for the token request?
choices: https://acme.identitynow.com/oauth/token
https://api.identitynow.com/acme/oauth/token
https://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
http://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
questions.answer: https://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
questions.explanation: The token endpoint lives on the tenant's API gateway host over HTTPS. Posting to the UI host is a common mistake, and plain HTTP is not accepted.

questions.stem: A web app uses the authorization code flow for tenant acme. Which URL should it send users to for sign-in?
choices: https://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/authorize
https://login.sailpoint.com/acme/authorize
https://acme.identitynow.com/api/authorize
https://acme.login.sailpoint.com/oauth/authorize
questions.answer: https://acme.login.sailpoint.com/oauth/authorize
questions.explanation: The authorize endpoint is on the tenant's login.sailpoint.com host, while the token exchange uses api.identitynow.com. The tenant name is a subdomain, not a path.

questions.stem: Users of tenant acme sign in to the user interface through the default SailPoint domain. Which address do they open?
choices: https://acme.api.identitynow.com
https://identitynow.com/acme
https://acme.identitynow.com
https://acme.sailpoint.com/ui
questions.answer: https://acme.identitynow.com
questions.explanation: The tenant UI is served at tenant.identitynow.com. The api host is for REST calls, and tenant names are subdomains rather than paths.

questions.stem: A tenant uses the vanity URL iga.acme.com for its user interface. A developer is unsure which token endpoint to use. What should the developer do?
choices: Send token requests to https://iga.acme.com/oauth/token
Ask the DNS team to point the vanity domain at the API gateway instead
Read the tenant's OAuth details from oauth/info on its API host
Use the vanity domain as the authorize and token host
questions.answer: Read the tenant's OAuth details from oauth/info on its API host
questions.explanation: A vanity URL changes the UI address but the token endpoint stays on tenant.api.identitynow.com; oauth/info lists the exact endpoints. Pointing DNS elsewhere would break the UI.

questions.stem: A team has a production tenant named acme and a sandbox named acme-sb. A script works in production. What must change to run it against the sandbox?
choices: Keep the production URL and add a sandbox header to each API call made
Use the sandbox's own hosts and an API client created in the sandbox
Keep the production client and change only the URL path
Use the production token, which also works in the sandbox
questions.answer: Use the sandbox's own hosts and an API client created in the sandbox
questions.explanation: Each tenant has its own hostnames and its own OAuth clients, so both the URL and the credentials change. Tokens are tied to the tenant that issued them.

questions.stem: An admin needs the exact tenant name to build API URLs but only knows the vanity address. Where in the UI can it be found?
choices: The Org Details section of the Admin Dashboard overview
The From address section in product branding
The source configuration of the authoritative source
The cluster page of the virtual appliance
questions.answer: The Org Details section of the Admin Dashboard overview
questions.explanation: The dashboard overview shows the org name used in tenant.api.identitynow.com. Branding and source pages do not list it.

questions.stem: Which address correctly sends a REST API call for tenant acme through the API gateway?
choices: A path on https://acme.login.sailpoint.com
A path on https://acme.api.identitynow.com
A path on https://api.acme.identitynow.com
A path on https://acme.identitynow.com/api
questions.answer: A path on https://acme.api.identitynow.com
questions.explanation: API calls go to the tenant's api.identitynow.com host. The login host is for sign-in, and swapping the order of tenant and api in the host name gives an address that does not exist.

questions.stem: Identity Security Cloud runs shared microservices for many customers. How does a service know which tenant an API request belongs to?
choices: The tenant is taken from the claims in the request's access token
Each tenant has its own copy of every microservice on its own server
The caller adds the tenant name as a query parameter on every call
The VA tags each request with the tenant before it reaches the cloud
questions.answer: The tenant is taken from the claims in the request's access token
questions.explanation: Tokens carry tenant claims, and the shared services process each request in that tenant's context. VAs are not in the path of API calls.

questions.stem: A developer tries to use an access token issued by the sandbox tenant against the production tenant. What happens?
choices: It is refused, since tokens only work on the tenant that issued them
The call succeeds, because both tenants belong to the same company account
The call succeeds with read access only on production data
The call is forwarded to the sandbox and runs there
questions.answer: It is refused, since tokens only work on the tenant that issued them
questions.explanation: Tokens are bound to their tenant, which keeps tenant data separate. Ownership by the same company does not merge tenants.

questions.stem: An architect asks why the API enforces rate limits even for a paying customer's busy integration. What is the BEST explanation?
choices: The limits are only applied when the tenant's VA is offline
Shared services need limits so one client cannot overload others
The limits stop customers from reading their own data too often each day
The limits apply only to tokens issued to Helpdesk users
questions.answer: Shared services need limits so one client cannot overload others
questions.explanation: In a multi-tenant platform, per-client limits keep one integration from degrading service for others. They apply regardless of VA state or user level.

questions.stem: An engineer aggregates a source and immediately searches for a new account, but it appears only a short time later. What explains this?
choices: The search index is rebuilt only once each night
Search results come from the VA cache, which syncs hourly
Processing is asynchronous, so search updates shortly after indexing
New accounts are hidden from search until a certification is completed
questions.answer: Processing is asynchronous, so search updates shortly after indexing
questions.explanation: Jobs and indexing run asynchronously, so search is updated shortly after processing rather than instantly. It is not a nightly rebuild.

questions.stem: Why must cloud-executed rules be submitted to SailPoint for review, when connector rules that run on the VA follow a different process?
choices: Cloud rules are written in a language SailPoint must translate
Cloud rules run on the customer's VA and need network approval
Cloud rules are visible to other tenants until SailPoint has reviewed them
They run inside the shared platform, so review protects all tenants
questions.answer: They run inside the shared platform, so review protects all tenants
questions.explanation: Code that runs in the shared cloud could affect other customers, so SailPoint reviews it before deployment. Connector rules run on the customer's own VA.

questions.stem: A company asks to delay a platform update until after its quarter-end. What should the engineer explain?
choices: The update can be skipped by turning off the tenant's VA cluster
Each tenant can pin its own platform version in the Admin UI
SailPoint updates every tenant continuously on its own schedule
The update applies only to sandbox tenants until approved
questions.answer: SailPoint updates every tenant continuously on its own schedule
questions.explanation: As a multi-tenant SaaS service, the platform is updated by SailPoint for everyone. Testing new behaviour in the sandbox is the customer's control.

questions.stem: A team wants one VA cluster to serve both its sandbox and production tenants to save servers. What is the correct design?
choices: Register the same VAs to both tenants with two key pairs
Deploy separate VAs for each tenant, as a VA serves one tenant
Use the production VAs and point sandbox sources at them
Let the sandbox use production's cluster during business hours
questions.answer: Deploy separate VAs for each tenant, as a VA serves one tenant
questions.explanation: Each VA is paired with one tenant's cluster and keys, so sandbox and production need their own. Sharing would also mix test and production traffic.

questions.stem: An application has no API, and its admins work from ServiceNow tickets. How should access changes reach them?
choices: Use a service desk integration so provisioning creates tickets
Use a Web Services connector against the app's database
Use an HTTP subscription that posts each change to the app's login page
Use a search subscription emailed to the app's admins
questions.answer: Use a service desk integration so provisioning creates tickets
questions.explanation: Service desk integration turns provisioning requests into tickets and tracks them. A Web Services connector needs an API the app does not have.

questions.stem: A workflow must call a partner's REST API to register each new hire. Which workflow step should the engineer use?
choices: The Send Email action addressed to the partner's support mailbox
The Compare Strings operator on the partner's URL
The HTTP Request action with the partner's authentication
A Loop operator over the partner's API pages
questions.answer: The HTTP Request action with the partner's authentication
questions.explanation: The HTTP Request action calls outside APIs with configurable method, headers and authentication. Operators only branch or repeat steps.

questions.stem: A company's HR database runs in its own data center with no internet exposure. How should Identity Security Cloud read it?
choices: A direct cloud connector that queries the database over the internet
An HTTP subscription that the database calls each night
An external workflow trigger called by the database
A JDBC source that runs through a virtual appliance on site
questions.answer: A JDBC source that runs through a virtual appliance on site
questions.explanation: Sources that are only reachable inside the network use VA-based connectors such as JDBC. A direct connector cannot reach a private database.

questions.stem: A SaaS application has a documented REST API but no dedicated SailPoint connector. Which option is BEST for account and entitlement management?
choices: A Web Services connector configured with the application's endpoints
A flat file source updated by hand each week
A service desk integration that opens a ticket per change
An EventBridge subscription that writes to the application
questions.answer: A Web Services connector configured with the application's endpoints
questions.explanation: The Web Services connector can call a REST API for aggregation and provisioning. Flat files and tickets add delay and manual work.

questions.stem: A data warehouse team needs a nightly copy of identity data for analytics. Which design is BEST?
choices: Giving the warehouse team the Admin level to export by hand
A request-response trigger that waits for the warehouse
Copying identity data from the VA's local storage
A scheduled job calling the APIs with a read-only API client
questions.answer: A scheduled job calling the APIs with a read-only API client
questions.explanation: A least-privilege API client can pull data on a schedule. VAs do not hold the identity store, and Admin rights for analysts break least privilege.

questions.stem: An application supports the SCIM 2.0 standard for users and groups. Which approach should the engineer consider FIRST?
choices: Onboard it with a JDBC connector
Onboard it as a delimited file source
Onboard it through email notifications
Onboard it with the SCIM 2.0 connector
questions.answer: Onboard it with the SCIM 2.0 connector
questions.explanation: SCIM is a standard provisioning API, so the SCIM connector can manage it directly. JDBC and files suit databases and exports.

questions.stem: A security team wants its SIEM to receive provisioning results as they happen. What is the BEST integration?
choices: A weekly search subscription emailed to the SIEM team
A role whose criteria match identities with recent changes
An event trigger subscription that sends events to the SIEM
A certification campaign that ends with a report
questions.answer: An event trigger subscription that sends events to the SIEM
questions.explanation: Event trigger subscriptions push events in near real time to a receiving endpoint. Weekly emails are too slow for monitoring.

questions.stem: Match each purpose to the valid host for tenant acme.

pairs.item: REST API calls through the gateway

questions.explanation: The UI, API gateway, token and authorize endpoints each use a tenant subdomain. Putting the tenant name in the path is not a valid format.

questions.stem: A network architect is reviewing VA communication. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: The VA starts all connections to the cloud over outbound HTTPS
Source credentials are encrypted with the VA cluster's key pair
The tenant pushes jobs into the VA through an inbound port
The VA stores the tenant's full identity database locally
A single VA can serve several tenants at once
answers: The VA starts all connections to the cloud over outbound HTTPS
Source credentials are encrypted with the VA cluster's key pair
questions.explanation: VAs poll outbound and decrypt credentials with their cluster key. They do not accept inbound jobs, hold the identity store or serve several tenants.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to send events to an external system with an HTTP subscription.
items: Pick the event trigger that matches the business event
Create an HTTP subscription with the receiver's HTTPS URL
Set basic or bearer authentication for the receiver
Add a filter so only relevant events are sent
Send a test invocation and confirm the receiver handles it
questions.explanation: The trigger and target come first, then authentication and filtering, then a test before the subscription goes live.
